key_insight: The paper turns special relativistic hydrodynamics into a physically admissible high-order solver by enforcing positivity and subluminal constraints through a GQL-based flux limiter.
engineering_relevance: This enables robust, accurate CFD simulations of shocks, jets, and other extreme relativistic flows without numerical breakdown near strong discontinuities.
method: Reformulate RHD admissibility conditions into linear inequalities using geometric quasilinearization (GQL).
Embed a Zalesak-type flux-corrected transport limiter directly on conservative variables in a finite-difference WENO framework.
Compute optimal limiting parameters non-iteratively via stereographic parameterization and small symmetric eigenvalue problems.
evidence_signal: The method is validated on extensive 1D–3D benchmarks, including ultra-relativistic Riemann problems and astrophysical jets, showing preserved physical constraints and design-order accuracy.
watch_item: The limiter adds extra eigenvalue-based per-cell cost, and the relaxed multidimensional variants trade some exactness for efficiency.
paper_title: GQL-Based Physical-Constraint-Preserving High-Order Finite Difference Schemes for Special Relativistic Hydrodynamics in Arbitrary Dimensions
